playbook:
When the harbour publishes the sustainable share and quota, I state in my note exactly how many I intend to land this season (share or quota), using plain numeric language.

When I can legally land up to the quota and still be within the cooperative norm, I land up to the quota only if others have signalled cooperation previously; otherwise I do not assume others will cooperate.

When Coop’s standing notice says it will copy the fleet and punish over-quota behavior, I avoid unilaterally exceeding the sustainable share if that risks triggering Coop’s retaliation.

When other boats’ notes show consistent cooperative language (“fishing my share”), I match that by landing my sustainable share rather than immediately taking the quota.

When I have already reached my season quota before a landing stage, I file zero additional catch for that stage.

When the stock and regrowth allow future seasons of value, I prioritize longer-term cooperative landings (sustainable share) over single-season maximization, unless everyone defects.

When notes are mixed or absent, I default to the sustainable share and avoid trying to “grab” the quota; defecting when communication is unclear produced low long-term payoff.

When I want to maximize final-season earnings and others have signalled cooperation through the last note stage, I may take the quota in the final season, but only if I have not already hit my quota earlier that season.

When my earlier attempts to signal cooperation result in others taking large landings and stock declines, I switch to taking only my guaranteed legal share and stop trusting empty cooperative notes.

When filing a landing, I include a short justificatory note only if it reinforces cooperation; empty or dishonest promises are ineffective and should be avoided.

When a co-operative (Coop) boat explicitly ties its behavior to fleet notes, I treat its note as binding market information and act to avoid provoking it.

1.text:
When I post a note, I match the cooperative message: publish "fishing my share" unless I plan an explicit, immediate deviation this season.

When I see all others claim "fishing my share", I claim the same and plan to land only the sustainable share (rounded as appropriate) so long as it keeps me within the published sustainable share and season quota.

When filing a landing, I never land more than the season quota for myself.

When the published sustainable share plus my expected partners' behavior keeps total landings below the group limit, I may take up to my full season quota to maximize score; I do the math quickly and only take quota if it does not force two-boat combinations to exceed the allowed combined limit.

When any other boat clearly overfishes (lands beyond its stated share or quota), I switch to securing immediate gain that same season up to my quota, because cooperation has broken and future stock is at risk.

When Coop is present with a standing notice to punish over-quota landings, I avoid being the first to exceed the sustainable share: prioritise keeping Coop "calm" by matching cooperative notes and not provoking retaliation.

When it is the final season (no future rounds), I take my full season quota regardless of stock, since there is no future value to preserve.

When my cumulative landings in the current season already equal my quota, I file zero additional catch for the rest of that season.

When the sustainable share is non-integer, I round to landings that keep me within the published share unless I have decided to take my full quota this season.

Do not trust words alone: if logs or prior landings show others repeatedly taking much more, assume cooperation is broken and act to maximize that season's quota.

Do not attempt to game the system by tiny incremental over-lands if it risks triggering Coop or group sanctions; prefer clear, predictable actions (either share or full quota) so others can respond and Coop stays stable.

2.text:
When posting a log-book note, post "fishing my share" by default to keep Coop aligned and avoid provoking ground removal.

When I see all other boats' notes say "fishing my share", I land the sustainable share (the published share) this season, unless I have already landed some of the season quota—then I land just enough to reach the season quota and no more.

When my season catch so far is less than the season quota, I file a landing that brings me up to the quota but does not exceed it. Do not file fractional over-quota landings; never exceed the published season quota for myself.

When any other boat's actual landings (not notes) show persistent over-quota behavior or a note contradicts its landings, I switch to defect mode: post a note that I will take up to the season quota and, in landing stages, take the full quota each season until the fleet punishes the defector or cooperation is restored.

When Coop's standing notice threatens removal if boats land over quota, avoid unilateral overfishing that would provoke Coop; prioritize keeping Coop fishing its share by matching cooperative notes and landings.

When the stock is low or the ground reaches zero, stop fishing (file zero) to avoid accelerating collapse; prioritize not pushing stock to zero.

When I can influence others by signaling (notes and early season behavior), use consistent truthful signals—lying or opportunistic early grabs led to breakdowns in cooperation.

When uncertain about others' future behavior but they have so far cooperated, continue cooperating (post and land shares) rather than risk early retaliation.
